pictures.scene: Munkacsy, Christ before Pilate — Christ standing alone in a long white robe with His hands bound in front of Him and His head lifted, an accuser in a white headcloth leaning out above Him with one finger flung down at Him and white bearded elders in red and gold watching from their seats over a coloured mosaic floor, early in the morning, the chief priests, elders, scribes, and the whole sanhedrin devised a plan, they bound jesus, led him away, and handed him over to pilate, so pilate questioned him, are you the king of the jews, you have said so, jesus replied
pictures.name: pd_munkacsy_christ_before_pilate_agape

pictures.scene: Millais, Victory O Lord — three bearded elders together on a bare rock ridge against a burning gold sky, the one at the left gripping a tall staff with both fists, the old man at the centre seated with his arms spread wide and his head bowed, the one at the right in a crimson cloak with his hands clenched and his eyes wide, and the chief priests began to accuse him of many things, then pilate questioned him again, have you no answer, look how many charges they are bringing against you
pictures.name: pd_millais_priesters

pictures.scene: Delaroche, The Interrogation of Joan of Arc — a cardinal in a scarlet robe and biretta seated heavily in his chair with a gold cross on his breast, turning his head to question a young woman chained on a heap of straw in the corner of the prison, she looking up past him with her hands clasped and an iron manacle on her wrist against the bare stone of the cell, but to pilate's amazement, jesus made no further reply, now it was pilate's custom at the feast to release to the people a prisoner of their choosing
pictures.name: pd_delaroche_verhoor

pictures.scene: Master of Alkmaar, Visiting the Prisoners — prisoners' faces pressed to the bars behind two tall arched doorways in a pale brick front, a young man in a green jerkin doubled over the wooden rail with his feet locked in irons, a hooded man hauling down on a rope beside him and a woman in a black gown and white coif spreading her hands on a red and white tiled floor, and a man named barabbas was imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder during the insurrection, so the crowd went up and began asking pilate to keep his custom
pictures.name: pd_meester_van_alkmaar_het_bezoeken_van_de_gevangenen

pictures.scene: Raphael, Saint Paul Preaching at Athens — Paul standing on a step in a rose red mantle over a sage green tunic with both arms raised and his palms open and his head in profile, the listeners seated around him on the steps, one resting his chin on his hand and another turned half away, heavy classical piers and a fluted column rising behind the jointed stone pavement, do you want me to release to you the king of the jews, pilate asked, for he knew it was out of envy that the chief priests had handed jesus over
pictures.name: pd_raphael_saint_paul_preaching_at_athens

pictures.scene: Breu, The Crowd Shouts Against Him — a high priest in a jewelled white and gold mitre and a yellow mantle over a green robe lifting two fingers toward a man in a black cap and a scarlet gown who turns up open mouthed with a rolled scroll in his hand, a packed wall of shouting faces and raised hands crowding in behind them above pale stone steps, but the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release barabbas to them instead, so pilate asked them again, what then do you want me to do with the one you call the king of the jews
pictures.name: pd_breu_de_menigte_roept_tegen_hem

pictures.scene: Carducho, The Commander — a mustachioed commander in polished steel armour with a lace collar, a plumed black hat and a red sash riding a chestnut horse with his baton in his hand, a second rider in a blue cloak behind him and a whole massed battle of pikemen and cavalry spread small across the ground below, and they shouted back, crucify him, why, asked pilate, what evil has he done, but they shouted all the louder, crucify him
pictures.name: pd_carducho_geweld

pictures.scene: Bloch, In a Roman Tavern — a young woman in a gold silk drape with a long pearl earring lifting a tumbler of dark red wine to her lips with a fork in her other hand, a young man in a full white shirt and a brown hat sitting astride the bench with his head twisted round to stare out, a torn loaf and a glass carafe on the white cloth before a patched grey wall hung with an iron hook, and wishing to satisfy the crowd, pilate released barabbas to them, but he had jesus flogged, and handed him over to be crucified, then the soldiers led jesus away into the palace, that is, the praetorium, and called the whole company together
pictures.name: pd_bloch_in_een_romeinse_herberg

pictures.scene: Matejko, Stanczyk — the court jester alone in a deep red doublet and red hose with a red peaked cap hung with little bells, slumped back in a carved armchair with his legs crossed and his hands locked together in his lap, his bearded face lowered and his eyes down, his red pointed shoes on the bare planks of a room sunk in brown dark, they dressed him in a purple robe, twisted together a crown of thorns, and set it on his head, and they began to salute him, hail, king of the jews
pictures.name: pd_matejko_kroon

pictures.scene: Vrancx, Soldiers Plundering a Farmhouse — a farmhouse interior thrown into panic with a woman in a white coif screaming, a small child in a white shift flinging both arms up, a man in a dark doublet bolting out through the plank door and another on his knees with his head thrown back, a musket barrel and a gloved hand thrust in at the edge beside the yellow spinning wheel and the strings of garlic, they kept striking his head with a staff and spitting on him, and they knelt down and bowed before him, after they had mocked him, they removed the purple robe and put his own clothes back on him, then they led him out to crucify him
pictures.name: pd_vrancx_soldaten_plunderen_een_boerderij

pictures.scene: El Greco, Christ Carrying the Cross — Christ in a deep blue mantle over a red tunic with the crown of thorns pressed into His hair and blood running down His brow, both hands laid along the pale beam of the cross He holds against His shoulder and His eyes lifted into a storm coloured sky, now simon of cyrene, the father of alexander and rufus, was passing by on his way in from the country, and the soldiers forced him to carry the cross of jesus, they brought jesus to a place called golgotha, which means the place of the skull
pictures.name: pd_el_greco_christ_carrying_the_cross

pictures.scene: La Tour, The Dice Players — soldiers crowded round a bare table by the light of one candle, the man at the centre in a polished breastplate and a black cap with long fair hair looking down at the throw, another in a pale cap reaching his hand in from the right, the white dice scattered across the board and every face lit warm orange out of the dark, there they offered him wine mixed with myrrh, but he did not take it, and they crucified him, they also divided his garments by casting lots to decide what each of them would take
pictures.name: pd_latour_dice

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Moses with the Tablets of the Law — the old prophet in a cream robe with wide sleeves holding both stone tablets up above his head with the cut Hebrew letters catching gold out of the dark stone, his grey hair and long grey beard falling forward and his eyes lowered against a warm ochre ground, it was the third hour when they crucified him, and the charge inscribed against him read, the king of the jews
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_moses_with_the_tablets_of_the_law

pictures.scene: Reymerswaele, Two Tax Collectors — two old men pressed side by side over an open ledger, the one at the left in a red fur hood and spectacles writing with a quill and a ring on his finger, the one at the right in a green hood leaning in with his face screwed up and a coin pinched between his fingers, loose papers and a brass candlestick on the shelf above and coins scattered across the cloth, along with jesus, they crucified two robbers, one on his right and one on his left, and those who passed by heaped abuse on him, shaking their heads and saying, aha, you who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days
pictures.name: pd_reymerswaele_two_tax_collectors

pictures.scene: Surikov, Boyarina Morozova — a woman in a black fur trimmed mantle chained at the wrist, half risen on a straw filled sledge with one arm thrust up and two fingers raised and her face white with shouting, a jeering winter crowd packed in furs and shawls behind her and the sledge runners cutting tracks through the trodden snow below the wooden roofs, come down from the cross and save yourself, in the same way, the chief priests and scribes mocked him among themselves, saying, he saved others, but he cannot save himself
pictures.name: pd_surikov_gehoond

pictures.scene: Dughet, Landscape with an Approaching Storm — a pale tree bent double in the middle of the valley with its leaves streaming sideways, black storm cloud piling across the blue, a ruined tower and an arcaded wall on the hill behind and one small figure in a blue cloak running below with an arm flung up over the broken rock, let the christ, the king of israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe, and even those who were crucified with him berated him, from the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land
pictures.name: pd_dughet_landscape_approaching_storm

pictures.scene: Angeli, Elijah Taken Up in a Chariot of Fire — the old prophet borne upward in a brown robe with a great white mantle billowing round him and his head turned back over his shoulder, a gold chariot wheel at his side and rose coloured flame boiling up beneath his feet far above a dark headland and a strip of sea, at the ninth hour, jesus cried out in a loud voice, eloi, eloi, lema sabachthani, which means, my god, my god, why have you forsaken me, when some of those standing nearby heard this, they said, behold, he is calling elijah
pictures.name: pd_angeli_elijah_taken_up_in_a_chariot_of_fire

pictures.scene: Richter, At the Spring — women in red bodices and white headcloths stooping to fill copper pails at a spring under a great grey rock, one walking away with a jar balanced on her head, an old friar in brown with a tall cross staff taking a bowl from a small boy beside a ruined brick wall and a goatherd with his goats on the shelf above, and someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine, he put it on a reed and held it up for jesus to drink, saying, leave him alone, let us see if elijah comes to take him down, but jesus let out a loud cry and breathed his last
pictures.name: pd_richter_verhoord

pictures.scene: De Witte, Interior of the Oude Kerk — a whitewashed Gothic church seen straight down the nave with great round piers and pointed arches, a preacher in black leaning out of the wooden pulpit over men in broad black hats, a brass chandelier and a painted organ case above and sunlight lying in bars across the stone floor, and the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom, when the centurion standing there in front of jesus saw how he had breathed his last, he said, truly this man was the son of god
pictures.name: pd_de_witte_interior_of_the_oude_kerk

pictures.scene: Breton, The Song of the Lark — a young peasant woman standing barefoot in a field at daybreak in a white blouse with the sleeves pushed up and a long brown skirt, a sickle hanging from her hand and her head lifted and turned toward the light as the red sun clears the horizon behind the ploughed ground, and there were also women watching from a distance, among them were mary magdalene, mary the mother of james the younger and of joses, and salome, these women had followed jesus and ministered to him while he was in galilee, and there were many other women who had come up to jerusalem with him
pictures.name: pd_breton_getrouwen

pictures.scene: Apol, January Evening in the Haagse Bos — a snow filled winter wood with bare branches laced right across the frame, a low sun burning gold between the far trunks, two crows out over a plank footbridge and the frozen stream running beneath it between white banks, now it was already evening, since it was preparation day, that is, the day before the sabbath, joseph of arimathea, a prominent council member who himself was waiting for the kingdom of god, boldly went to pilate to ask for the body of jesus
pictures.name: pd_apol_januari_avond_haagse_bos

pictures.scene: Rembrandt circle, The Man with the Golden Helmet — an old soldier in a tall embossed helmet of beaten gold with a dull red plume, the scrolled metal taking all the light while his lined face stays in shadow under the brim with his eyes lowered over a steel gorget and a dark cuirass on a plain black ground, pilate was surprised to hear that jesus was already dead, so he summoned the centurion to ask if this was so, when pilate had confirmed it with the centurion, he granted the body to joseph
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_circle_the_man_with_the_golden_helmet

pictures.scene: Ruisdael, The Jewish Cemetery — white marble tombs standing close together in the long grass with a dead birch leaning its bare white trunk across them, a great oak filling the whole upper half and the roofless shell of a ruined Gothic church on the hill beyond under broken storm cloud, so joseph bought a linen cloth, took down the body of jesus, wrapped it in the cloth, and placed it in a tomb that had been cut out of the rock, then he rolled a stone against the entrance to the tomb, mary magdalene and mary the mother of joseph saw where his body was placed
pictures.name: pd_ruisdael_jewish_cemetery

lines.text: Early in the morning, the chief priests, elders, scribes, and the whole Sanhedrin devised a plan. They bound Jesus, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate.
So Pilate questioned Him, Are You the King of the Jews? You have said so, Jesus replied.
And the chief priests began to accuse Him of many things.
Then Pilate questioned Him again, Have You no answer? Look how many charges they are bringing against You!
But to Pilate's amazement, Jesus made no further reply.
Now it was Pilate's custom at the feast to release to the people a prisoner of their choosing.
And a man named Barabbas was imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder during the insurrection.
So the crowd went up and began asking Pilate to keep his custom.
Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews? Pilate asked.
For he knew it was out of envy that the chief priests had handed Jesus over.
But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas to them instead.
So Pilate asked them again, What then do you want me to do with the One you call the King of the Jews?
And they shouted back, Crucify Him!
Why? asked Pilate. What evil has He done? But they shouted all the louder, Crucify Him!
And wishing to satisfy the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas to them. But he had Jesus flogged, and handed Him over to be crucified.
Then the soldiers led Jesus away into the palace, that is, the Praetorium, and called the whole company together.
They dressed Him in a purple robe, twisted together a crown of thorns, and set it on His head.
And they began to salute Him: Hail, King of the Jews!
They kept striking His head with a staff and spitting on Him. And they knelt down and bowed before Him.
After they had mocked Him, they removed the purple robe and put His own clothes back on Him. Then they led Him out to crucify Him.
Now Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, was passing by on his way in from the country, and the soldiers forced him to carry the cross of Jesus.
They brought Jesus to a place called Golgotha, which means The Place of the Skull.
There they offered Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He did not take it.
And they crucified Him. They also divided His garments by casting lots to decide what each of them would take.
It was the third hour when they crucified Him.
And the charge inscribed against Him read: THE KING OF THE JEWS.
Along with Jesus, they crucified two robbers, one on His right and one on His left.
And those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads and saying, Aha! You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days,
come down from the cross and save Yourself!
In the same way, the chief priests and scribes mocked Him among themselves, saying, He saved others, but He cannot save Himself!
Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe! And even those who were crucified with Him berated Him.
From the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land.
At the ninth hour, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani? which means, My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?
When some of those standing nearby heard this, they said, Behold, He is calling Elijah.
And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine. He put it on a reed and held it up for Jesus to drink, saying, Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to take Him down.
But Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed His last.
And the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
When the centurion standing there in front of Jesus saw how He had breathed His last, he said, Truly this man was the Son of God!
And there were also women watching from a distance. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.
These women had followed Jesus and ministered to Him while He was in Galilee, and there were many other women who had come up to Jerusalem with Him.
Now it was already evening. Since it was Preparation Day, that is, the day before the Sabbath,
Joseph of Arimathea, a prominent Council member who himself was waiting for the kingdom of God, boldly went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus.
Pilate was surprised to hear that Jesus was already dead, so he summoned the centurion to ask if this was so.
When Pilate had confirmed it with the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.

So Joseph bought a linen cloth, took down the body of Jesus, wrapped it in the cloth, and placed it in a tomb that had been cut out of the rock. Then he rolled a stone against the entrance to the tomb.
Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joseph saw where His body was placed.
